Correct Answer: C. Döhle body
•	A. Cabot ring: Seen in red blood cells as remnants of mitotic spindle, not in neutrophils.
•	B. Heinz body: Present in red blood cells due to denatured hemoglobin.
•	C. Döhle body: Pale blue cytoplasmic inclusions seen in neutrophils, especially in infections.
•	D. Pappenheimer body: Iron-containing granules seen in red blood cells.

records.solution:
Answer: b) Aptt
Intrinsic pathway: XII → XI → IX + VIII → X (common pathway)
•	This pathway is assessed by aPTT (activated partial thromboplastin time)
Extrinsic pathway: Tissue Factor (III) + Factor VII → Activation of Factor X
•	This pathway is assessed by PT (Prothrombin Time)

records.solution:
Answer: c) Aptt
•	Heparin primarily affects the intrinsic pathway and thus prolongs the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT). 
•	aPTT is used to monitor the anticoagulant effect of heparin therapy to ensure therapeutic levels without excessive bleeding risk.
•	PT and INR monitor Warfarin therapy (extrinsic pathway).
•	Bleeding time assesses platelet function, not coagulation factor activity.
